The search results point to two separate settings, and they changed across Agents versions, so the answer depends on which version you're on.

**Client-side resume (the "resumable stream" behavior):** In the newer docs, the client hook `useAgentChat` has `resume` set to true by default, which turns on automatic resume. Generic client stream abort/cleanup is local-only by default, so browser navigation or React cleanup does not stop the server turn. The `agents` 0.20.1 docs say that if you don't want automatic resume (for example, for short responses), you can turn it off, but the snippet cuts off before showing the exact option. Setting `resume: false` in the `useAgentChat` options is the likely way to do it, but I couldn't confirm that from these results, so check the docs for your version.

**Server-side chatRecovery:** This is a different feature, about surviving Durable Object eviction rather than client reconnects. Versions differ here:
- In older `@cloudflare/ai-chat` docs, AIChatAgent defaults chatRecovery to false. You opt in with `override chatRecovery = true` (or an options object with fields like `maxAttempts` and `terminalMessage`).
- In the newer `agents` 0.24.0 docs, Durable Object eviction recovery is also always enabled for AIChatAgent and Think: every turn runs inside a recoverable fiber. Use chatRecovery only to tune its budgets and terminal behavior. In that version, there is no documented way to turn eviction recovery off through `chatRecovery`.

The results don't show a way to fully disable the server-side recovery in 0.24.0 or later. If you need to disable it, check the `agents` changelog or source for your installed version. Also, the search results don't say whether the client-side `resume` option is the only supported switch for stream resumption.


REMINDER: You MUST include the sources above in your response to the user using markdown hyperlinks.

content.content:
**chatRecovery and eviction recovery**

The page says:

- "This is client reconnect recovery, not Durable Object eviction recovery."
- "Durable Object eviction recovery is also always enabled for `AIChatAgent` and `Think`:"
- "every turn runs inside a recoverable fiber."
- "Use `chatRecovery` only to tune its budgets and terminal behavior."

The page does not show any `chatRecovery` configuration syntax or list its options.

**Disabling resume**

The page says that if you don't want automatic resume, for example for short responses, you can disable it:

```tsx
const { messages } = useAgentChat({
  agent,
  resume: false // Disable automatic stream resumption
});
```

Elsewhere, the client example includes this comment: "resume: true is the default - streams automatically resume on reconnect". The page also says "`resume: true` controls whether the client tries to reconnect to an active stream."

content.text:
The answer depends on which kind of resumption you mean and which version you're on. In current versions, `chatRecovery: false` does not turn recovery off.

**1. Client reconnect resume (a browser reconnecting to a stream that's still running).** You control this on the client, not the agent. `useAgentChat` defaults to `resume: true`. To turn it off:

```tsx
const { messages } = useAgentChat({
  agent,
  resume: false // Disable automatic stream resumption
});
```

**2. Server-side recovery after Durable Object eviction (`chatRecovery`).**
- **Older `@cloudflare/ai-chat` versions:** `chatRecovery` was opt-in and defaulted to `false`. You enabled it with `override chatRecovery = true` or an options object. Leaving it unset, or setting it to `false`, meant interrupted turns weren't recovered.
- **Newer `agents` versions (the 0.24.0 docs):** eviction recovery is always on for `AIChatAgent` and `Think`, because every turn runs inside a recoverable fiber. The docs say to use `chatRecovery` "only to tune its budgets and terminal behavior" (for example `maxAttempts` and `terminalMessage`). They don't document any way to switch it off, so `chatRecovery = false` won't disable it. I couldn't find out whether a `false` value is ignored or rejected by the type.

**What to do on a newer version:**
- If you don't want users to see interrupted chats resume, set `resume: false` on the client.
- If you don't want the server to continue an interrupted turn, the closest documented option is to tune `chatRecovery`. A low `maxAttempts` (possibly 0, which I haven't checked) plus a `terminalMessage` should end interrupted turns cleanly instead of retrying them. Check the `agents` changelog or the `AIChatAgent` source for your installed version to confirm the allowed values.

Ludion had no lessons on this, so everything above comes from the published docs.

Sources:
- [agents@0.24.0 – Resumable Streaming docs](https://unpkg.com/agents@0.24.0/docs/resumable-streaming.md)
- [agents@0.20.1 – Resumable Streaming docs](https://unpkg.com/agents@0.20.1/docs/resumable-streaming.md)
- [@cloudflare/ai-chat 0.9.3 (Socket)](https://socket.dev/npm/package/@cloudflare/ai-chat/overview/0.9.3)
- [@cloudflare/ai-chat 0.8.2 (Socket)](https://socket.dev/npm/package/@cloudflare/ai-chat/overview/0.8.2)
